series.description: 'Outstanding deposits' show position of deposits held by banks at the end of the period (30th June or 31st December). Deposits are the amount held in various types of deposit accounts by bank; such as demand deposits; time and saving deposits. Deposits include all types of deposits excluding interbank deposits; placements and margin deposits (deposits held by banks as collateral against letters of credits; letters of guarantees).

series.name: Outstanding Deposits of Government from all Pakistan
series.description: This includes Federal Government; Provincial & Local Governments deposits and advances. Further; disbursements to Government (Federal; Provincial & Local) are made by bank branches located in various regions/Provinces; while in case of deposits; the bank branches located in the various regions/Provinces have mobilized the deposits from the Government (Federal; Provincial & Local). Similarly; disbursements to eight main borrowers (Foreign; Govt.; NFPSEs; NBFCs; Private Sector; Trust Fund; Personal and Others) are made by bank branches located in various regions/Provinces; while in case of deposits; the bank branches located in the various regions/Provinces have mobilized the deposits from these eight categories.

series.name: Outstanding Deposits of NFPSEs from all Pakistan
series.description: These are the non-financial resident corporations which are controlled by government; which may be exercised through ownership of more than half the voting shares; legislation; decree; or regulations that establish specific corporate policy or allow the government to appoint the directors.

series.name: Outstanding Deposits of NBFIs from all Pakistan
series.description: NBFIs (Nonbank Financial Institutions) are categorized into groups of development finance institutions; leasing companies; investment banks; modaraba companies; housing finance companies; mutual funds; venture capital companies ; discount houses; stock exchanges ; exchange companies and insurance companies etc.

series.name: Outstanding Deposits of Private Sector (Business) from all Pakistan
series.description: This is that part of the economy which is run for private business profit and is not controlled by the state. This includes the majors sectors like Agriculture; Manufacturing etc.

series.name: Outstanding Deposits of Trust Funds and other NPIs from all Pakistan
series.description: This includes the Private Trusts and Non-profit Institution; Non-government Organization (NGOs)/ Community Based and Organizations (CBOs).

series.name: Outstanding Deposits of Personal/Individual Customers from all Pakistan
series.description: This includes Bank Employees and Consumer Financing which are classified under advances; while in case of deposits; Salaried Persons; Self-employed and Other Persons (House-wives; students etc) are included.

series.name: Outstanding Deposits of Other Depositors n.e.c from all Pakistan
series.description: This includes all those which are not classified elsewhere.

series.name: Outstanding Deposits of Foreign Constituents from all Pakistan
series.description: This covers the transactions with the non-residents working in our economy. This includes Officials (Embassies consulates; foreign missions); Business (Corporations working in Pakistan for short periods as construction companies) and Personals (Students; travelers).

series.description: These data series display the data of loans to textile sector by Banks and DFIs operating in Pakistan. These loans are classified according to the ISIC sector of the borrower (Manufacture of Textiles; Weaving/Spinning/Finishing; Manufacture of made up textiles; etc); the category of financing (WC i.e. Working Capital and FI i.e. Fixed Investment) and the type of loan information that is being displayed (OS i.e. Outstanding Loans or GD i.e. Gross Disbursement).  Some explanations of other acronyms are: LTF-EOP is a SBP sponsored subsidized lending scheme for long term projects; EFS is also an SBP refinance scheme for short term export-oriented projects Important Note: The data for 2019-12-31 does not contain the information for DFIs. DFIs information only starts from June-2020 onwards

These loans are classified according to the ISIC sector of the borrower (Manufacture of Textiles; Weaving/Spinning/Finishing; Manufacture of made up textiles; etc); the category of financing (WC i.e. Working Capital and FI i.e. Fixed Investment) and the type of loan information that is being displayed (OS i.e. Outstanding Loans or GD i.e. Gross Disbursement).  Some explanations of other acronyms are: LTF-EOP is a SBP sponsored subsidized lending scheme for long term projects; EFS is also an SBP refinance scheme for short term export-oriented projects Important Note: The data for 2019-12-31 does not contain the information for DFIs. DFIs information only starts from June-2020 onwards

These loans are classified according to the ISIC sector of the borrower (Manufacture of Textiles; Weaving/Spinning/Finishing; Manufacture of made up textiles; etc); the category of financing (WC i.e. Working Capital and FI i.e. Fixed Investment) and the type of loan information that is being displayed (OS i.e. Outstanding Loans or GD i.e. Gross Disbursement).  Some explanations of other acronyms are: LTF-EOP is a SBP sponsored subsidized lending scheme for long term projects; EFS is also an SBP refinance scheme for short term export-oriented projects Important Note: The data for 2019-12-31 does not contain the information for DFIs. These loans are classified according to the ISIC sector of the borrower (Manufacture of Textiles; Weaving/Spinning/Finishing; Manufacture of made up textiles; etc); the category of financing (WC i.e. Working Capital and FI i.e. Fixed Investment) and the type of loan information that is being displayed (OS i.e. Outstanding Loans or GD i.e. Gross Disbursement).  Some explanations of other acronyms are: LTF-EOP is a SBP sponsored subsidized lending scheme for long term projects; EFS is also an SBP refinance scheme for short term export-oriented projects Important Note: The data for 2019-12-31 does not contain the information for DFIs. These loans are classified according to the ISIC sector of the borrower (Manufacture of Textiles; Weaving/Spinning/Finishing; Manufacture of made up textiles; etc); the category of financing (WC i.e. Working Capital and FI i.e. Fixed Investment) and the type of loan information that is being displayed (OS i.e. Outstanding Loans or GD i.e. Gross Disbursement).  Some explanations of other acronyms are: LTF-EOP is a SBP sponsored subsidized lending scheme for long term projects; EFS is also an SBP refinance scheme for short term export-oriented projects Important Note: The data for 2019-12-31 does not contain the information for DFIs. DFIs information only starts from June-2020 onwards

These loans are classified according to the ISIC sector of the borrower (Manufacture of Textiles; Weaving/Spinning/Finishing; Manufacture of made up textiles; etc); the category of financing (WC i.e. Working Capital and FI i.e. Fixed Investment) and the type of loan information that is being displayed (OS i.e. Outstanding Loans or GD i.e. Gross Disbursement).  Some explanations of other acronyms are: LTF-EOP is a SBP sponsored subsidized lending scheme for long term projects; EFS is also an SBP refinance scheme for short term export-oriented projects Important Note: The data for 2019-12-31 does not contain the information for DFIs. These loans are classified according to the ISIC sector of the borrower (Manufacture of Textiles; Weaving/Spinning/Finishing; Manufacture of made up textiles; etc); the category of financing (WC i.e. Working Capital and FI i.e. Fixed Investment) and the type of loan information that is being displayed (OS i.e. Outstanding Loans or GD i.e. Gross Disbursement).  Some explanations of other acronyms are: LTF-EOP is a SBP sponsored subsidized lending scheme for long term projects; EFS is also an SBP refinance scheme for short term export-oriented projects Important Note: The data for 2019-12-31 does not contain the information for DFIs. These loans are classified according to the ISIC sector of the borrower (Manufacture of Textiles; Weaving/Spinning/Finishing; Manufacture of made up textiles; etc); the category of financing (WC i.e. Working Capital and FI i.e. Fixed Investment) and the type of loan information that is being displayed (OS i.e. Outstanding Loans or GD i.e. Gross Disbursement).  Some explanations of other acronyms are: LTF-EOP is a SBP sponsored subsidized lending scheme for long term projects; EFS is also an SBP refinance scheme for short term export-oriented projects Important Note: The data for 2019-12-31 does not contain the information for DFIs. DFIs information only starts from June-2020 onwards

series.name: Other Items (net)
series.description: Other items (net) encompasses all those activities of the banking system; which may not be specified by sector. OIN are valued on a net basis and are shown on the asset side of NDA. They include a range of items such as physical assets of bank (on assets side) capital and reserves (as a liability side); profit or losses of the central bank; valuation adjustment in respect of SBP¿s NFA resulting from exchange rate changes entailing unrealized profit or losses and any other items that have not been classified elsewhere. They also include the impact of SBP¿s money market operation. If SBP inject liquidity through reverse repo/discounting it increases its other assets and thereby an expansionary impact on its OIN. On the other hand; SBP¿s repo sales (mop-up) increases its other liabilities and thereby contraction in its OIN

series.name: Weighted Average rate of Public banks
series.description: This data gives weighted average lending and deposit rates of all scheduled banks operating in Pakistan on various parameters. Banks are divided into 4 different types: Public; Private; Foreign; and Specialized. This data shows separate numbers for flows and stocks for both loans and deposits. series.name: BOP4-Overall Balance
series.description: The difference between the value of transactions in which money leaves a country and the value of transactions in which money enters it. A positive¿overall balance¿means more money leaves a country; while a negative¿overall balance¿indicates the opposite. Or the positive overall balance represents that how much of the country¿s reserve have been used for net payments during the period and the negative overall balance shows how much of the country¿s reserve have been accumulated after the net payments during the period.

series.name: BOP4-Net Foreign Assets
series.description: The negative amount of net foreign assets shows that how much of the country¿s reserve have been used for net payments during the period and the positive value shows how much of the country¿s reserve have been accumulated after the net payments during the period .

series.name: BOP4-Net Foreign Assets-Use of Fund Credit and Loans

series.name: BOP4-Net Foreign Assets- Foreign Currency Accounts
series.description: Net amount of export bills

series.name: BOP4-Net Foreign Assets- Net Changes in Reserves
series.description: The negative amount of reserves shows that how much of the country¿s reserve have been used for net payments during the period and the positive value shows how much of the country¿s reserve have been accumulated after the net payments during the period .

series.name: BOP4-Net Foreign Assets- Net Changes in Reserves-SBP
series.description: The negative amount of reserves shows that how much of SBP's reserve have been used for net payments during the period and the positive value shows how much of SBP¿s reserve have been accumulated after the net payments during the period .

series.name: BOP4-Net Foreign Assets- Net Changes in Reserves-DMB

series.name: BOP-Net Errors and Omissions
series.description: Net errors and omissions constitute a residual category needed to ensure that accounts in the balance of payments statement sum to zero. Net errors and omissions are derived as the balance on the financial account(including reserves and related items) minus the balances on the current and capital accounts

series.name: BOP-Overall Balance
series.description: The difference between the value of transactions in which money leaves a country and the value of transactions in which money enters it. A positive¿overall balance¿means more money leaves a country; while a negative¿overall balance¿indicates the opposite. OR The positive Overall balance represents that how much of the country¿s reserve have been used for Net payments during the period and the negative overall balance shows how much of the country¿s reserve have been accumulated after the Net payments during the period.

series.name: BOP-Reserves and Related Items
series.description: The negative amount of reserves and related items shows that how much of the country¿s reserve have been used for Net payments during the period and the positive value shows how much of the country¿s reserve have been accumulated after the Net payments during the period.

series.name: BOP-Reserve Assets
series.description: The negative amount of reserves shows that how much of the country¿s reserve have been used for Net payments during the period and the positive value shows how much of the country¿s reserve have been accumulated after the Net payments during the period .

series.name: BOP-Use of Fund Credit and Loans
series.description: The negative amount of use of fund credit and loans shows borrowing while positive value shows repayments.

series.name: BOP-Exceptional Financing
series.description: Exceptional financing combines financial transactions under financial arrangements made by the authorities (or by other sectors fostered by the authorities) of an economy to meet balance of payments needs

series.name: BOP-SBP Gross Reserves
series.description: This series shows gross foreign exchange reserves with SBP.For current month's data on SBP Gross Reserves; please see 'Monthly Summary of Balance of Payments as per BPM6' dataset.

series.name: Imports Payments by Banks
series.description: Total imports payments of goods made through banks

series.name: Freight & Insurance
series.description: Insurance and freight is an expense paid by a seller to cover the insurance and freight of a buyer's order while it is in transit. Currently; it is estimated as 2.7% of total import payments of goods through banks.

series.name: Imports Payments Banks (fob)
series.description: Import payments of goods through banks on 'Free on Board' basis is calculated by subtracting freight & insurance from total import payments through banks

series.name: Other Imports
series.description: 1: Other Imports include goods procured in ports by carriers; refund/rebate; imports under foreign economic assistance (grants and loans); trade credit and other miscellaneous items as per BPM6.2: Import of oil/petroleum under financing from international financial institutions/foreign governments has been classified in the relevant country since Jul-22 which was previously classified in Other Imports.

series.name: Total Imports BOP
series.description: Total imports as per balance of payments is calculated by combining 'total imports of goods through banks' & 'other imports' and subtracting 'freignt and insurance' from it.

series.name: Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (Base Year: 2000)
series.description: Nominal Effective Exchange rate (NEER) is an index of the bilateral nominal exchange rates of one country relative to its  major trading partners or basket of currencies. The bilateral nominal exchange rate index with each trading partner weighted by that country's' share in imports; exports; or total foreign trade.

series.name: Real Effective Exchange Rate (Base Year: 2000)
series.description: Real Effective Exchange rate (REER) is an index of the price of a basket of goods in one country relative to the price of the major trading partners or basket currencies. The prices of these baskets expressed in the same currency using the nominal exchange rate with each trading partner. The price of each trading partner's basket weighted by its share in imports; exports; or total foreign trade.

series.name: Total Number of Roshan Digital Accounts (RDAs) Opened Since Inception to Date
series.description: This refers to the cumulative number of Roshan Digital Accounts (RDAs) opened by Non-Resident Pakistanis (NRPs) since the initiation of the RDA program. It includes all accounts opened globally by NRPs across all participating banks up to the reference date.

series.name: Total Funds Received from Abroad into RDAs Since Inception to Date
series.description: This represents the cumulative amount of foreign remittances received into Roshan Digital Accounts (RDAs) by Non-Resident Pakistanis (NRPs) from abroad since the initiation of the RDA program. The figure reflects the aggregate value of all remittances in various currencies (such as USD; PKR; EUR; GBP; etc.); converted to US dollars using the daily weighted average customer exchange rates.

series.name: Total Funds Repatriated Abroad from RDAs Since Inception to Date
series.description: This represents the cumulative amount of funds remitted from RDAs to foreign countries since the initiation of the RDA program. The figures; originally in multiple currencies; are converted to US dollars using the daily weighted average customer exchange rates.

series.name: Total RDA Funds Utilized Locally Since Inception to Date
series.description: This represents the cumulative funds from RDAs that have been used for non-repatriable purposes within Pakistan. These include local transfers to non-repatriable accounts; ATM cash withdrawals; utility and educational bill payments; mobile top-ups; merchant transactions; and other domestic uses. These funds are no longer considered obligations. The figures; originally in multiple currencies; are converted to US dollars using the weighted average customer exchange rates.

series.name: Total RDA Funds Repatriated and Utilized Locally Since Inception to Date
series.description: This figure represents the total value of funds repatriated abroad plus funds utilized locally in Pakistan by RDA holders since the program¿s inception. Local utilization covers all non-repatriable expenditures; including domestic payments and transactions.

series.name: Total Outstanding Net Repatriable Liabilities
series.description: This value represents the net amount of repatriable funds currently held within RDAs and available for transfer abroad. It includes all outstanding positions across investment and savings instruments linked with RDAs but excludes any profit; gain; or loss data.

series.name: Outstanding Investments in Conventional Naya Pakistan Certificates (NPCs)
series.description: This represent the total outstanding value of investments made by RDA holders in Conventional Naya Pakistan Certificates (NPCs); which are government issued fixed income instruments. The figures; originally denominated in multiple currencies (PKR; USD; GBP; and EUR); have been converted to US dollars using month end exchange rates.

series.name: Outstanding Investments in Islamic Naya Pakistan Certificates (INPCs)
series.description: This represent the total outstanding value of investments made by RDA holders in Islamic Naya Pakistan Certificates (INPCs); which follow Shariah compliant investment principles. The figures; originally denominated in multiple currencies (PKR; USD; GBP; and EUR); have been converted to US dollars using month end exchange rates.

series.name: Market Value of Investments in the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX)
series.description: This refers to the total market value of stocks held by RDA investors in the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX); as of the reporting date. The original values; calculated in Pakistani Rupees (PKR); are converted into US dollars using month end exchange rate.

series.name: Remaining Balances Available in Roshan Digital Accounts (RDAs)
series.description: This represents the total value of funds that remain available in RDAs; including those placed in Term Deposit Receipts (TDRs). It includes all currencies consolidated and converted into US dollars using month end exchange rates.

series.name: Outstanding Other Liabilities (Excluding NPCs; INPCs; Stocks; and Balances)
series.description: This figure covers all other outstanding financial liabilities not covered under NPC Investments (Conventional); NPC Investments (Islamic); Roshan Equity Investments or Balances in Accounts. It includes investments in government securities like treasury bills;PIBs; Sukuk; mutual funds; and real estate holdings. All values are aggregated from different currencies and converted into US dollars using month end exchange rates.

series.name: Workers Remittances
series.description: This series shows the total of workers remittances received from non-resident Pakistanis in a month

series.name: Seasonally adjusted Worker Remittance
series.description: This series shows the seasonally adjusted workers' remittances received from non-resident Pakistanis in a month

series.name: Gold reserves
series.description: This series contains end period market value of gold held as reserve assets (monetary gold) by the monetary authority.

series.name: Net Reserves with SBP
series.description: This series contains SBP reserves excluding unsettled claims on Reserve Bank of India; Cash Reserve Requirement/Special Cash Reserve Requirement (CRR/SCRR); Net Asian Clearing Unit ACU (from June 2020 onwards); foreign currency cash holdings and IMF reserve position (from June; 2020 onwards).

series.name: Total SBP Reserves
series.description: This series is the sum of SDR holdings; cash foreign currency; Nostro balances; net ACU balances and IMF reserve position excluding CRR/SCRR (compiled as per IMF balance of payments manual guidelines). Total SBP reserves series available on annual (end June) basis from 1948 to 1971 and on monthly basis onwards.

series.name: Special Drawing rights holdings
series.description: This series contains end period balances of Special Drawing rights holdings(SDR).

series.name: Nostro balances of SBP
series.description: This series contains end period balances of Nostro accounts of SBP including CRR/SCRR and sinking funds. CRR included from Jun 1999 to Jun 2005; excluding CRR from July 2005 onwards.

series.name: Cash Foreign Currency with SBP-BSC
series.description: This series contains end period balances of foreign currency in cash held with SBP BSC.

series.name: Net Asian clearing unit balances
series.description: This series contains Asian clearing unit (ACU) accounts net balances.

series.name: IMF reserve position
series.description: This series contains end period balances of IMF reserve position.

series.name: Cash reserve requirement and special cash reserve requirement (CRR/SCRR)
series.description: This series contains end period balances of cash reserve requirement CRR and special cash reserve requirement SCRR.

series.name: Net Reserves With Banks
series.description: This series contains Total FE-25 deposits excluding trade financing (in align with Foreign Exchange Reserves compiled by DMMD).

series.name: Total Banks Reserves
series.description: This series contains FE-25 deposits; trade Nostro; placement abroad other than FE-25 excluding trade financing; FE-25 placement in Pakistan and others (compiled as per IMF balance of payments manual guidelines).

series.name: FE-25 deposits of banks
series.description: This series contains end period balances of Foreign Currency Accounts Opened under FE-Circular 25 of 1998.

series.name: Trade Nostro of banks
series.description: This series contains end period balances of Banks Currency and Deposits abroad excluding FE-25 Balances held Abroad and Cash in Foreign Currency.

series.name: Place abroad(other than FE-25) of banks
series.description: This series contains placement abroad other than FE-25.

series.name: Trade Finance from FCA
series.description: This series contains end period balances of Export and Import Financing from Foreign Currency Accounts.

series.name: FE-25 Placements of banks in Pakistan
series.description: This series contains end period balances of FE-25 balances placed with banks in Pakistan.

series.name: FE-25 utilization-Others
series.description: This series contains end period utilization of FE-25 Balances Not specified elsewhere.

series.name: Total Reserve Assets
series.description: This series is sum of gold and foreign exchange reserves with SBP and foreign exchange reserves with scheduled banks . Series discontinued from October 2024 and onward as the data has been discontinued from SBP Statistical Bulletin.

series.name: Total Liquid FX Reserves
series.description: This series is sum of net reserves with SBP and banks. Series discontinued from October 2024 and onward as the data has been discontinued from SBP Statistical Bulletin.
