series.name: Ordinary share capital of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This represents the total paid-up capital against issue of ordinary shares. These are amount of capital actually paid by the shareholder¿s to the institution for acquiring its shares. It includes shares paid in cash (subscribed/right issued); issued as bonus shares and shares issued for consideration other than cash (e.g. for settlement of receivables/debts or debts redeemable into stock etc.).

series.name: Surplus on revaluation of fixed assets of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Revaluation of fixed assets is a technique that may be required to accurately describe the true value of the capital goods that a business owns. The revaluation surplus has been included in equity because capital goods like property; plant and equipment's participate directly in the revenue generation and transferred directly to retained earnings.

series.name: Shareholders' equity of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This item purports to represent the total stake of the shareholders in the business and has been obtained by adding the ordinary share capital to the surplus.

series.name: Preference shares of non-financial listed companies
series.description: As the name indicates these are ordinary shares of a company and pays a fixed dividend (whether the company is earning profit or making loss during operation); but its shareholders have no voting privilege. In case of liquidation of the company its status is normally considered prior to the status of ordinary shareholders. The difference between ordinary shares and preference shares is as follows: a) Ordinary shareholder will receive dividend; which varies according to the prosperity of the company but preference shareholder will receive a fixed amount dividend every year. b) Ordinary shareholder has a right of voting in the company¿s annual general meeting while the preference shareholder has no voting right. c) Ordinary shareholders have to claim on the net assets of the company in case of liquidation; while the claim of the preference shareholders is paid earlier.

series.name: Debentures bonds/certificates of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are bonds/certificates issued by a company to raise funds for long-term period (generally more than one year) for a specific purpose; sometimes convertible into stock. At present; debentures have been replaced by TFC¿s (Term Finance Certificates).

series.name: Loans from Banks; NFBIs; Specialized Banks; Foreign loans & Vendors¿ etc. payables by non fina. Lstd Co.'s
series.description: The liabilities; which are required to be discharge after a period of more than one year from the date of balance sheet; are termed as other fixed liabilities or loan capital. They may consist of the following items: (i) Loans from financial institutions. (ii) Loans from non bank financial institutions. (iii) Loans from specialized financial institutions (iv) Foreign loans (v) Vendors¿ account

series.name: Total fixed liabilities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It is the sum of the preference shares; debentures and other fixed liabilities.

series.name: Total capital employed of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It is the sum of shareholders¿ equity and total fixed liabilities.

series.name: Gearing ratios of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This item shows the proportion that the fixed loan capital bears to the total capital employed. Where there is preference capital; there is an item of Gearing i.e.; the fixed loan capital plus the preference capital as the ratio of the total capital employed. The justification for taking the preference capital together with the fixed liabilities is that; from the ordinary shareholders' point of view; both items represent a fixed charge on the profits. Total capital employed is shareholders equity plus total fixed liabilities. Gearing becomes inapplicable when the shareholders' equity becomes zero or negative.

series.name: Shareholders' equity to share capital ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It gives an idea of relationship of shareholders' equity to ordinary share capital.

series.name: Break-up value of ord shares of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It is obtained by dividing the amount of shareholders equity by the number of ordinary shares.

series.name: Liquid Assets held by non-financial listed companies
series.description: Broadly speaking; liquid assets comprise of all assets like cash; bank balance; marketable security; etc.; which are easily realizable almost at book value. While there can not be two opinions regarding the status of cash; current accounts and government securities in this context; the treatment of savings and fixed deposits and of shares of joint stock companies not quoted on stock exchange leaves the analyst in doubt. The classification of borderline cases had therefore; to be made partly in keeping with the objective of the analysis and partly on one¿s own subjective judgment. For this study; liquid assets that are also sometimes referred to as liquid capital have been bifurcated as cash and investments and comprise of the following items: - (i) Cash in hand (ii) Cash in transit (iii) Current deposits (iv) Saving deposits (v) Call deposits (vi) Fixed deposits (vii) Deposits held abroad (viii) Government and corporate securities (ix) Savings and Unit Trust Certificates (x) Debentures stock of local or foreign companies

series.name: Cash & bank balance of non-financial listed companies
series.description: A cash balance indicates that a company has cash on hand and can use that cash however it wishes. Cash includes more than just the physical traditional bills and coins.

series.name: Short term investments made by non-financial listed companies
series.description: Unlike long term investments; short term investments have to be matured within the same accounting cycle. The basic motive of such an investment is to earn profits or capital gains for short term period. They may include: (i) Short-term stocks (ii) Short -term bonds (iii) Short -term investment in real estate (iv) Short-term Government and corporate securities (v) Short-term Savings and Unit Trust Certificates (vi) Short-term Debentures stock of local or foreign companies

series.name: Other cur. assets incl. stores & spare; trade deposit & prepayments etc. of non-fin. listed cos.
series.description: These are all remaining items of current assets left from the above coverage; but remained in the balance sheet. These include (i) Book debts including bad and doubtful debts (ii) Stores; spare parts and loose tools (iii) Loans and advances (iv) Work in progress(current) (v) Advances and prepayments etc. (vi) Balances due to tax department (vii) Tax refundable (viii) other receivables

series.name: Current assets of non-financial listed companies
series.description: An asset is to be a current asset; which can be readily convertible into cash or equivalent without any significant loss in value. The current assets comprise of liquid assets; inventories and other current assets.

series.name: Current liabilities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: All liabilities; which are required to be discharge within one year; are termed as current liabilities. Alternatively; these cover those obligations whose liquidation is expected to be made out of current assets. They are usually incurred in the normal course of business and are required to be paid at fairly definite dates. The current liability consists of the following items.

series.name: Total liabilities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This item pertains to sum of total fixed liabilities and current liabilities except shareholder's equity.

series.name: Net current assets held by non-financial companies listed at PSX
series.description: It has been obtained by deducting the amount of current liabilities from current assets.

series.name: Contractual liabilities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This item pertains to all secured debentures; long-term loans; finance lease; short term secured loans and bank overdraft (Interest bearing secured loans).

series.name: Current Ratio of non-financial listed  companies
series.description: This item tells a lender about the liquidity of the assets and as a result its ability to pay the short- term debts.

series.name: Net liquid assets of non-financial companies listed at PSX
series.description: This is the difference of liquid assets and the current liabilities.

series.name: Fixed assets at cost of non-financial listed companies
series.description: In contra distinction to current assets; fixed assets consist of items; which are not readily convertible into cash during the course of normal operations of an enterprise. These items are not subject to periodical exchange through sales and purchases. Fixed assets are of permanent nature and are not normally liquidated or intended to be turns into cash except in the form of depreciation; which is added to the cost of goods sold. The following balance sheet items are included in the category of fixed assets: -(a) Real Estate (i) Freehold and leasehold land (ii) Factory and office buildings (iii) Residential buildings (iv) Capital projects in progress at cost (b) Plant; Machinery and Rolling Stock (i) All types of plant and machinery used for production and not for sale (ii) Crockery; cutlery; silverware and enamelware in hotels (iii) Construction tools (iv) Livestock in farming company (v) Cars; lorries; trucks; ships; launches etc.(vi) Railway siding and trolley lines (vii) Computers and other electronic equipment's. vi(c) Furniture; Fixtures; Fittings and Allied Equipment (i) Electric fans; refrigerators; air conditioners; electric heating; sanitary and other fittings (ii) Laboratory equipment (iii) All types of office furniture's and equipment (iv) Advertising; fixtures and fittings

series.name: Fixed assets after Dec Acc Dep of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Deducting the accumulated depreciation from the fixed assets of the company gives this item.

series.name: Depreciation for the year of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It includes all the depreciation charges to the profit and loss account during the year. Owing to the absence of uniform accounting standards; depreciation is a subjective item and very from company to company. It is important for the analyst to know what effect such variation could have on the net profit.

series.name: Depreciation rate of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This item is simple depreciation rate and is intended to give some idea of the company's practice with regard to depreciation. Since there are so many items in the fixed assets schedule; it is not practicable to calculate depreciation rate for all the items individually. Therefore; an aggregate depreciation rate for all the item taken together has been worked out. The method is to take total depreciation provided during the financial year and dividing it by the written down value of the total fixed assets at the beginning of the financial year. The result is expressed in percentage.

series.name: Total assets of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This item is sum of fixed assets at cost after deducting accumulated depreciation; and current assets.

series.name: Gross Sales made by non-financial listed companies
series.description: OPERATION:This item represents the sale proceeds of the company. Sales revenue is classified as local sales and export sales.

series.name: Local sales in gross sales made by non-financial listed companies
series.description: Sales within own country are called local or domestic sales.

series.name: Export sales in gross sales made by non-financial listed companies
series.description: Export sale means 'a transaction entered into between a reporting exporter and a foreign buyer.

series.name: Gross profit of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Subtracting cost of sales from sales revenue arrives at gross profit.

series.name: Gen & administrative expenses of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are total expenses that are incurred on the operational activities of a company except financial expenses and include: (i) Cost of sales (ii) Administrative and general expenses (iii) Selling and distribution expenses (iv) Other expenses

series.name: Operating profit of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Subtracting overhead and other expenses from gross sales and adding thereto-non-operating income gives operating profit.

series.name: Operating ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: D3 as % of D1

series.name: Financial expenses of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are interest expense incurred on borrowing of long and short terms loans. It includes the following items; (i) Mark-up and interest on long term loan(ii) Mark-up and interest on debentures and redeemable capital(iii) Mark-up and interest on short term loan (iv) Interest on private loan(v) Financial charges against assets subject to finance lease(vi) Interest and mark-up on supplier credit(vii) Interest on worker's profit participation fund.(viii) Bank charges and commission.(ix) Excise duty on long and short-term finance.(x) Discounting charges on receivables.(xi) Exchange losses.

series.name: Fin expenses ratio of oper profit of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This shows the ratio of financial expenses to operating profit. It identifies how much weight the company will bear from its operating profit before reaching to the net profit before tax. Smaller ratio is a good for a company.

series.name: Financial Exp to gross sales ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It shows the ratio of financial expenses to gross sales. Lowering the ratio indicates the financial discipline of the company and the increasing ratio indicates that the company is facing financial expense burden out of its gross sales revenue

series.name: Financial expenses to contractual liabilities ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It shows cost incurred (interest/mark up paid) on contractual liabilities.

series.name: Expenses of non-financial listed companies
series.description: An expense is the cost of operations that a company incurs to generate revenue. As the popular saying goes; ¿it costs money to make money.¿ Common expenses include payments to suppliers; employee wages; factory leases; and equipment depreciation.

series.name: Expenses as percent of shareholders equity of non-financial listed companies
series.description: D10 as % of A3

series.name: Net Profit before tax provision of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It is the profit earned by the company during the year before tax provision.

series.name: Net profit as percent of Sales  of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It is worked out by dividing the net profit before tax by the shareholders¿ equity; expressing the result in percentage.

series.name: Tax provision of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It is provision of taxation made on current year's profit.

series.name: Tax prov to net pre-tax profit of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It shows the portion of net profit set aside for tax provisions.

series.name: Sundry debtors to gross sales of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It is the ratio of outstanding credit (all sales receivables) to the total sale proceeds of the company. Higher the percentage; the company is increasing its debtors and credit risk and reducing its liquidity position.

series.name: Earning per ordinary share of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It has been arrived by dividing the net profit (before/after tax) by the number of ordinary shares.

series.name: before tax provision of non-financial listed companies
series.description: D12/No. of ordinary shares

series.name: after tax provision of non-financial listed companies
series.description: (D12-D14)/No. of ordinary shares

series.name: Net profit to shareholders'  equity of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It is worked out by dividing the net profit before tax by the shareholders' equity; expressing the result in percentage.

series.name: Total amount of dividend of of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It is the total dividend including interim dividend distributed or proposed to be distribute out of the current year's profit

series.name: Dividend ratio to equity of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This item has been worked out by dividing the total amount of dividend by the shareholders¿ equity; expressing the result in percentage

series.name: Dividend cover ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: The ratio of net profit after tax to total amount of dividend.

series.name: Total bonus shares issued by non-financial listed companies
series.description: This is the total amount of bonus shares issued to the shareholders as appropriation net profit after tax of the company during the year.

series.name: Increase/decrease in capital employed of non-financial companies listed at PSX
series.description: The difference in value of total capital employed (i.e.; share capital; surplus; preference capital; debentures and other fixed liabilities) at the beginning of the year and the corresponding figures at the end of the year and shown as increase (+)/ decrease (-).

series.name: Retention in business of non-financial  companies listed at PSX
series.description: This item is obtained by deducting the provision for the tax and the total dividend distributed or proposed to be distributed from the net profit for the year.

series.name: Self-financing ratio of non-financial companies listed at PSX
series.description: The ratio expresses the amounts retained in business as percentage of increase/ decrease in the capital employed.

series.name: Finance from outside of non-financial companies listed at PSX
series.description: The difference between the increase in the capital employed and the retention in the business is the finance from out side the company. It is possible for this item to be negative. Indeed in some circumstances it is also possible for the increase in the capital employed as well as the retention in business to be negative; for instance where dividends are distributed not out of the current earnings but out of the reserves.

series.name: Depreciation for the year plus retention in business of non-financial companies listed at PSX
series.description: Depreciation for the year is added in retention in business it reflects; total funds that corporation generates internally for investment in the modernization and expansion of plant and equipment.

series.name: Depreciation for the year plus changes in capital employed of non-financial companies listed at PSX
series.description: Depreciation for the year is added in the difference of two successive years' figures of total capital employed.

series.name: Cash flow ratio of non-financial companies listed at PSX
series.description: This ratio has a purpose somewhat similar to the self-financing ratio described under F.3 the only difference being that it takes into account the amount of depreciation.

series.name: No. of Companies listed at PSX
series.description: Total number of companies covered in the analysis for the year.

series.name: Non-current assets of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Non-current assets are assets whose value will not be realized within a period of one year since they are not easily converted into cash. The assets are recorded on the balance sheet; and they include property; plant and equipment; intellectual property; intangible assets; long term investments; long term loans and advances and other long-term assets.

series.name: Capital work in progress of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Capital work in progress consists of the unfinished products in a production process. They are not yet complete but either being fabricated or waiting in a queue or storage. They must be accounted for as funds (capital) that have been invested for future enhancement in production.

series.name: Operating fixed assets at cost of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are owned by an enterprise engaged in production of items (directly or indirectly); which will be available for sale. These are not readily convertible into cash during the course of normal operations of an enterprise. These assets are not subject to periodical exchange through sales and purchases. Fixed assets are of permanent nature and are not normally liquidated or intended to turn into cash except in the form of depreciation; which is added to the cost of goods sold. The following balance sheet items are included in the category of fixed assets: - (a)    Real Estate  (i)      Freehold and leasehold land  (ii)     Factory and office buildings (iii)    Residential buildings  (iv)   Capital projects in progress at cost  (b)   Plant; Machinery and Rolling Stock  (i)     All types of plant and machinery used for production and not for sale  (ii)    Crockery; cutlery; silverware and enamelware in hotels (iii)    Construction tools (iv)   Livestock in farming company (v)   Cars; lorries; trucks; ships; launches etc. (vi)  Railway siding and trolley lines (vii) Computers and other electronic equipment(c)   Furniture; Fixtures; Fittings and Allied Equipment (i)    Electric fans; refrigerators; air conditioners; electric heating; sanitary and other fittings. (ii)      Laboratory equipment (iii)   All types of office furniture¿s and equipment (iv)   Advertising; fixtures and fittings

series.name: Operating fixed assets after deducting accumulated depreciation of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Deducting the accumulated depreciation from the operating fixed assets of the company gives this item.

series.name: Intangible assets of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Intangible assets are defined as identifiable assets that cannot be seen; touched or physically measured; which are created through time and/or efforts and that are identifiable as a separate asset. The possible items are:(i) Copyrights(ii) Patents(iii) Trademarks(iv) Goodwill(v) Exploration accounts (vi) Knowledge accounts(vii)  Computer software accounts

series.name: Long term investments of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Investment is acquisition of financial; physical or technology based assets by an investor for their potential future income; return; yield; profits; or capital gains. The long-term investments account differs largely from the short-term investments account in that the short-term investments will most likely be sold; whereas the long-term investments may never be sold in the short run. They may include:(i) Long-term stocks(ii) Long-term bonds(iii) Long-term investment in real estate (iv) Long-term Government and corporate securities (v) Long-term Savings and Unit Trust Certificates (vi) Long-term Debentures stock of local or foreign companies

series.name: Investments of non-financial listed companies in their subsidiaries
series.description: A subsidiary is a company with majority voting stock that is more than 50% share of ordinary paid up capital and controlled by another company; usually referred to as the parent company or the holding company. A subsidiary is partly or completely owned by the parent company; which holds a controlling interest in the subsidiary company.

series.name: Investments of non-financial listed companies in associates
series.description: An associate company is a corporation whose parent company possesses only a minority stake in the ownership of the corporation. An associate company is partly owned by another company or group of companies. The parent company or companies do not consolidate the associate company's financial statements.

series.name: Long-term deposits; loans/adv. lent; sec. and deferred costs etc. of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These include all residual non-current assets left from the above coverage; but remain in the balance sheet. Possible items may be: (i) Deferred costs; (ii) Long-term deposits; (iii) Long- term loans and advances; (iv) Security deposits

series.name: Long term loans(lent) and advances of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are loans given to any business partner or subsidiary/associate company or advances to employee or a vender and supplier to supply of goods and services in future. These loans and advances are for longer period i.e. are given for more than a year.

series.name: Long term deposits inc. security deposit of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Long term deposit include security deposit with a service provider company (i.e. e.g. WAPDA; SSGC) or deposit with a company against a finance lease or line of credit. These deposit are of long term nature i.e. of more than a year.

series.name: Current assets of  non-financial listed companies
series.description: Current assets are all the assets of a company that are expected to be sold or used as a result of standard business operations over the next year. Typical current assets include cash; cash equivalents; accounts receivable; stock inventory; marketable securities; pre-paid liabilities; and other liquid assets.

series.name: Cash & bank balance of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Cash & bank balances is an integral part of a company's overall operations. It consists of:(i)    Cash in hand (ii)    Cash in transit(iii)   Current deposits(iv)   Saving deposits(v)   Saving deposits and call deposits(vi)   Deposits held abroad

series.name: Inventories of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Inventory or stock refers to the goods and materials that a business holds for the ultimate purpose of sale after processing; which consists of

series.name: Raw material in inventory of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It is basic substance in its natural; modified; or semi-processed state; used as an input to a production process for subsequent modification

series.name: Work in progress in inventory of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It refer the work in process; is the sum of all costs put into the production process to manufacture products that are partially completed.

series.name: Finished goods in inventory of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Finished goods are goods that have been completed by the manufacturing process; or purchased in a completed form; but which have not yet been sold.

series.name: Trade Debt / accounts receivables of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This refers to an entity from which amounts are due for goods sold or services rendered or in respect of contractual obligations and also termed: debtor; trade debtor; and account receivable.

series.name: Short term loans and advances receivable of non-financial listed companies
series.description: In general; when a company gives any loan to its employee or its sister concerns or to its director which are recoverable in future as per term and conditions mentioned there in. This loan is considered as of company's asset and is recorded as short term loan if time of recovery of loan is matured within one year. Advances on the other hand are given by a company to its employee or its sister concerns or to its director for particular purposes against either goods are to be received by company or services are to be received in near future.

series.name: Short term investments made by non-financial listed companies
series.description: Unlike long term investments; short term investments have to be matured within the same accounting cycle. The basic motive of such an investment is to earn profits or capital gains for short term period. They may include:(i) Short-term stocks(ii) Short -term bonds(iii) Short -term investment in real estate (iv) Short-term Government and corporate securities (v) Short-term Savings and Unit Trust Certificates (vi) Short-term Debentures stock of local or foreign companies

series.name: Other curr. assets incl. stores & spare; trade deposit & prepayments etc. of non-fin. listed cos.
series.description: These are all remaining items of current assets left from the above coverage; but remained in the balance sheet. These include:(i) Book debts including bad and doubtful debts; (ii) Stores; spare parts and loose tools; (iii) Work in progress(current); (iv) Trade deposit and prepayments; (v) Balances due to tax department(vi) Tax refundable(vii) other receivables

series.name: Stores & spares in other current assets held by non-financial listed companies
series.description: Spare parts and loose tools are not part of any fixed assets but facilitate the process of production.

series.name: Trade deposits & pre-payments in other current assets held by non-financial listed companies
series.description: Trade Deposits are used to cover any potential losses in the event that the market moves against a given trade position whereas prepayments are settlement of debts or installment payments before its official due date

series.name: Total Assets/Equity & Liabilities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This item is sum of current and non-current assets or Sum of total liabilities (current and non-current) and Equity. It is also called Size of Balance sheet of a company.

series.name: Shareholders' Equity of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This item purports to represent the total stake of the shareholders in the business and is obtained by adding the ordinary share capital to the reserves and also surplus on revaluation of fixed assets.

series.name: Issued; Subscribed & Paid up capital of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This represents the total subscribed and paid-up capital against issue of ordinary shares. These are amounts of capital actually paid by the shareholders to the institution for acquiring its shares. It includes shares paid in cash (subscribed/right issued); issued as bonus shares and shares issued for considerations other than cash (e.g. for settlement of receivables/debts or debts redeemable into stock etc.).

series.name: Ordinary Shares of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Ordinary shareholders represent equity ownership in a company and entitled to vote into matters of the company in proportion to their percentage ownership in the company. ¿Ordinary shareholders are entitled to receive dividends if any are available after dividends paid to the preferred shareholders (if any).¿ They are also entitled to share as residual economic value of the company and stood last in line after bondholders and preferred shareholders for receiving business proceeds in case of company default to pay its obligations. At the end it may be expressed as that ordinary shareholders are considered unsecured creditors.

series.name: Preference shares of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Preferred Shares generally have dividends that must be paid out before dividends to common stockholders and the shares usually do not have voting rights. The precise details as to the structure of preferred stock are specific to each corporation. However; the best way to think of preferred stock is as a financial instrument that has characteristics of both debt (fixed dividends) and equity (potential appreciation). The difference between ordinary shares and preference shares is as follows: (a)  Ordinary shareholder receive dividend; which varies according to the prosperity of  the company but preference shareholder will receive a fixed amount dividend every year. (b) Ordinary shareholder has a right of voting in the company's annual general meeting while the preference shareholder has no voting right. (c) Ordinary shareholders have a residual claim on the net assets of the company in case of liquidation; while the claim of the preference shareholders is paid earlier.

series.name: Total reserves of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It is calculated by aggregating all kinds of reserves except depreciation reserve and reserve for bad and doubtful debts plus the balance of profit and loss account.

series.name: Capital Reserve of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These funds are allocated only to be spent on the capital expenditure projects/ future expansionary projects for which they were initially intended; excluding any unforeseen circumstances. These include:(a) Share premium reserves(b) Merger reserves(c)Development reserves(d) Reserve for issue of bonus shares (e) Reserve for re-issue of forfeited shares (f) Capital gain on sale of fixed assets(g) Dividend  equalization reserves(h) Non-controlling interest (minority interest)(i) Fair value Reserve(j) Subordinated Loans(k) Interest rate swap revaluation reserve(l) Hedge reserve(m) Advance against subscription for right shares(n) Undistributed percentage return reserve (o) Exploration and evaluation reserve(p) Investment revaluation reserve(q) Share deposit money(r) Exchange difference on translation of foreign subsidiaries(s) Statutory Reserve(t) Gain on re-measurement of forward foreign exchange contracts- cash flow hedge

series.name: Revenue Reserve of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This is that part of the profit that has been not given to the shareholders but retained in the business for future growth. These include:(a) General reserves(b) Un-appropriated reserves(c) Retained reserves(d) Reserves on profit & loss account(e) Deferred income (f) Retained Earnings

series.name: Unappropriated profit(loss) / retained earnings in revenue reserves of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Un-appropriated retained earnings consist of any portion of company profit/loss account that are not classified as appropriated retained earnings. Un-appropriated retained earnings cannot be allocated for a specific purpose; such as factory construction or marketing. They are generally passed on to shareholders in the form of dividends

series.name: Surplus on revaluation of fixed assets of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Revaluation of fixed assets is a technique that may be required to accurately describe the true value of the capital goods that a business owns. The revaluation surplus has been included in equity because capital goods like property; plant and equipment participate directly in the revenue generation and transferred directly to retained earnings.

series.name: Non-Current Liabilities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Noncurrent liabilities; also known as long-term liabilities; are obligations listed on the balance sheet that become due beyond twelve months in the future; as opposed to current liabilities which are short-term debts with maturity dates within the following twelve month period.

series.name: Long term borrowings of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Long-term borrowing in accounting; form part of a section of the balance sheet that lists liabilities not due within the next 12 months including loans and finance lease etc.

series.name: Long term secured loans in long term borrowing of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are liabilities which are required to be discharged after a period of more than a year from the date of balance sheet and are obtained on the basis of secured collaterals. These include:(i) Loans from financial institutions. (ii) Loans from non-bank financial institutions. (iii) Loans from specialized financial institutions (iv) Redeemable capital finance(v) foreign loans (vi) Vendors account

series.name: Long term unsecured loans in long term borrowing of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are liabilities which are required to be discharged after a period of more than a year from the date of balance sheet and are obtained without any secured collaterals. These include: (i) Loan to various organizations by governments.(ii) Loan to a company by directors(iii) Long term loan by creditors(iii) Long term loan by suppliers

series.name: Long term lease finance in long term borrowing of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are liabilities for assets being acquired through lease financing from a financial institution for period of more than one year depending on the specification of asset being leased. For example; commercial property usually has leases for five or more years; while residential property often carries long term leases for more than one year. A long-term lease locks in the price one pays for the asset; which is usually advantageous because prices often trend upward. These include: i) Assets under lease finance ii) Lease finance obligation

series.name: Subordinated loans/Sponsor's loans in non-current liabilities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Subordinated loan is a security loan that ranks below than other loans with regard to claims on a company's assets or earnings. Subordinated loan is also known as a junior security.  In the case of borrower default; creditors who own subordinated loan won't be paid out until after senior debt holders are paid in full. A sponsor'fs loan allows a parent to borrow on behalf of a subordinated company and take full responsibility for the loan. The sponsor loan is under the name of the sponsor borrower only.

series.name: Debentures/TFCs (bonds payable) of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are bonds/certificates issued by a company to raise funds for long-term period (generally more than one year) for a specific purpose (usually for capital expenditures); sometimes convertible into stock. At present; debentures have been replaced by TFCs (Term Finance Certificates)/Sukuks bonds.

series.name: Employees benefit obligations of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These include benefits provided either to employees or their dependents; and may be settled by payments (or the provision of goods or services) made either directly to the employees; their spouses; children; other dependents. Its constituents are:  (i) Employees salaries (ii)  Employees gratuity fund (iii)  Pension fund. (iv)  Staff compensated absences (v) Staff retirement benefits

series.name: Def. liabilities/ tax; Long term/key deposits and retention money of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are residuals of non-current liabilities left from the above coverage; but remained in the balance sheet of the company. These include: (i) Deferred liabilities (ii)  Deferred liabilities/ taxation (iii) Long term deposits/key deposits (iv) Retention money payable

series.name: Current Liabilities  of non-financial listed companies
series.description: All liabilities; which are required to be discharged within one year; are termed as current liabilities. Alternatively; these cover those obligations whose liquidation is expected to be made out of current assets. They are usually incurred in the normal course of business and are required to be paid at fairly definite dates.

series.name: Trade credit & other accounts payables  of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Small businesses generally use accounts payable as their largest source of financing. Accounts payable or trade credit are what businesses owe to their suppliers of inventory; products; and other types of goods that are necessary to operate the business.

series.name: Trade credits in Trade credit & other accounts payables of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Trade credit is the credit facility extended to a company by supplier who let the company to by now and pay letter or a service that has been acquired but not paid so for due to credit facility given by the provider.

series.name: Short term Borrowing of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Short-term borrowing account shown in the current liabilities portion of a company's balance sheet. These accounts are made up of any debt incurred by a company that is due within one year. The debt in this liabilities account is usually made up of short-term bank loans taken out by a company; among other types.

series.name: Short term secured loans in short term borrowing of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are loans which are to be matured within the year and have been obtained against secured collaterals. These consist of: (i) Secured short term running finance. (ii) Short term loan from bank

series.name: Short term unsecured loans in short term borrowing of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are loans which are to be matured within the year and have been obtained against unsecured collaterals. These consist of: (i) Short term loan to various organizations by governments. (ii) Short term loan to a company by directors (iii) Short term loan by creditors (iv) Short term loan by suppliers

series.name: Short term lease finance in short term borrowing of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are liabilities for assets being acquired through lease financing from a financial institution for period up to one year depending on the specification of asset being leased.

series.name: Current portion of non-current liabilities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: The current portion of long term liabilities are amount of principal that will be due within one year of the date of the balance sheet. These includes: (i) Current maturities of secured long term loan. (ii) Current maturities of redeemable capital finance (iii) Current maturities of lease finance

series.name: Payments due incl. taxes; staff retirement dues; loans; deposits & adv. etc of non-financial listed cos.
series.description: These are all remaining items of current liabilities left from the above coverage; but remained in the balance sheet. These include:(a) Sundry Creditors (i) For expenses (ii)  For other finance  (iii) Bills payable  (iv) Advances from customers against orders (b)  Payment become due but outstanding (i) Income tax payable (ii) Proposed; unpaid and unclaimed dividends (iii) Estimated liabilities in respect of outstanding claims whether due or intimated  (iv) Gratuities becoming payable (v) Provident Fund becoming payable  (vi)  Current installment and interest payable on fixed liabilities  (vii) Provision for taxation estimated on current profits (viii) Workers profit participation fund  (c)  Loans; Deposits and Advances (i) Loans secured by stock or other current assets (ii) Bank overdrafts and other unsecured loans  (iii) Short term loans acquired against the security of fixed assets  (iv)  Unsecured loan from directors; parent company; and subordinate loan (v)    Due to managing agents   (vi)   Advances by directors  (vii)  Guarantee and security deposits of customers and staff

series.name: Interest / markup payables in other current liabilities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Interest payable is the interest expense that has been incurred (has already occurred) but has not been paid as of the date of the balance sheet. Interest payable does not include the interest for periods after the date of the balance sheet.

series.name: Taxes payable in other current liabilities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Taxes payable are the amount of money a company owes in federal; provincial and municipal taxes. Harmonized sales tax (HST); income taxes and property taxes all contribute to taxes payable and appear under liabilities on the balance sheet. Taxes payable are a current liability; and are payable within a normal operating cycle of one year.

series.name: Net Sales made by non-financial listed companies
series.description: This item represents the sale proceeds of the company netting off all components of expenses associated with sales. Sales revenue is classified as local sales and export sales.

series.name: Local sales (Net) in total net sales of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Local sales is cover net of local revenues after adjusting sales tax; sales discounts; federal excise duties etc.

series.name: Export sales (Net) in total net sales of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Export sales covers net of export sales after adjusting export rebates and excise duties etc.

series.name: Cost of sales of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Cost of sales includes the direct costs attributable to the production of the goods sold by a company. This amount includes the materials cost used in creating the goods along with the direct labor costs used to produce the good.

series.name: Cost of material in cost of sales of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This includes cost of all raw and other processing materials incurred in the production of finished goods; which are available for sale of the company.

series.name: Salaries and wages in cost of sales of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This includes the sum of all wages and employee benefits paid to the labor/employee engaged in production/processing of the finished or final goods of the company.

series.name: Overhead expenses in cost of sales of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This include all of the costs that a factory incurs; other than direct costs and allocate the costs of manufacturing overhead to any inventory items that are classified as work-in-process or finished goods. These include: (i) Depreciation of factory equipment (ii) Quality control and inspection (iii) Indirect materials and supplies (iv) Repair expenses (v) Indirect materials and supplies

series.name: Gross profit / (loss) of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Gross profit is arrived at by subtracting cost of sales from sales revenue.

series.name: General; administrative and other expenses of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These expenses consist of the combined payroll costs (salaries; commissions; and travel expenses of executives; sales people and employees); and advertising expenses that a company incurs. This is usually understood as a major portion of non-production related costs.

series.name: Selling & distribution expenses in general and administrative expenses of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are non-production cost; but directly related with the revenue generation of saleable goods; i.e. cost incurred to mobilize goods from factory outlet to the market palace. These include: (a) Distribution expenses (b) Brokerage expenses (c) Salary; wages and commission expenses (d) Discount expenses (e) Selling expenses (f) Forwarding expenses (g) Advertisements and promotions

series.name: Advertisement & promotions in selling & distribution expenses of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Advertisements and promotion covers amount used by the company for product advertisements for both print and electronic media.

series.name: Administrative and other expenses of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These expenses are also non-production costs and fixed in nature. The company is obliged to pay these expenses which are permanent in nature until the structure of the company is not affected. These include: (a) Postage; telegram and telephone expenses (b) Conveyance and travelling expenses (c) Salary; wages and other benefits (d) Depreciation expenses (e) All other expenses not covered in administrative and distribution expenses

series.name: Corporate social responsibilities in administrative and other expenses of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Generally this heads covers amount paid for community developments and in most cases companies serve community in the form of donations.

series.name: Other income/(loss) arose from non-core business of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It treats these money flows differently depending on the activities that are responsible for them. 'Other Income' on an income statement usually refers to money that comes in from activities outside the company's core operations. It also cover share of income received from subsidiaries/associate companies in case where consolidated accounts are used for parent company.

series.name: Earning before Interest; depr & tax (EBIT) of non-financial listed companies
series.description: EBIT measures the profit a company generates from its operations; making it synonymous with 'operating profit.' By ignoring tax and interest expenses; it focuses solely on a company's ability to generate earnings from operations; ignoring variables such as the tax burden and capital structure. Mathematically it is calculated as: EBIT= Gross Profit less general administrative & other expenses plus  other incomes.  It is to be noted that EBIT may not be comparable with operating profit where a parent company shares the income received from profit/(loss) account of its subsidiaries into its own balance sheet (minority interest).

series.name: Financial expenses of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are expenses incurred due to borrowing of financial assets (short / long term loans) and acquisition of financial services by a company during an accounting period. It consists of interest paid expenses on loan/debts plus: (a) Interest and mark-up on supplier credit (b) Interest on worker¿s profit participation fund. (c) Bank charges and commission (d) Excise duty on long and short-term finance (e) Discounting charges on receivables (f) Exchange commission expenses

series.name: Interest expenses in financial expense of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are interest expenses incurred on borrowing of long and short terms loans. These include the following items;  (i)   Mark-up and interest on long term loan (ii)  Mark-up and interest on debentures and redeemable capital (iii) Mark-up and interest on short term loan (iv) Interest on private loan

series.name: Profit/(loss) before taxation of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It is the profit earned by the company during the year before tax.

series.name: Tax expenses of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Tax expenses are almost 'ordinary; necessary; and reasonable' expenses that is necessary to declare income of a business entity.

series.name: Current tax expenses in the tax expense of non-financial listed companies
for the current year tax expenses in total tax expense of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are amount of tax of current year period

series.name: prior year tax expenses paid in current year in total tax expense of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These amount of taxes include the period previous beyond the current year

series.name: Deferred tax payable in total tax expense of non-financial listed companies
series.description: A deferred tax liability is an account on a company's balance sheet that is a result of temporary differences between the company's accounting and tax carrying values.

series.name: Profit / (loss) after tax of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It is the profit earned by the company during the year after all its expenses; charge-offs; depreciation and taxes have been subtracted.

series.name: Cash dividends of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It is the total dividend including interim dividend distributed or proposed to be distributed out of the current year's profit.

series.name: Bonus shares / stock dividends of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This is the total amount of bonus shares issued to the shareholders as appropriation of net profit after tax of the company during the year.

series.name: Net cash flows from operating activities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Cash flow from operating activities (CFO) is an accounting item indicating the money a company brings in from regular business activities; such as manufacturing and selling goods or providing a service.  It include earnings before interest and taxes plus depreciation minus taxes. Cash From Operating Activities = EBIT + Depreciation  Operating activities include the production; sales and delivery of the company's product as well as collecting payment from its customers. This could include purchasing raw materials; building inventory; advertising; and shipping the product; Under IAS 7; operating cash flows include:  ¿ Receipts from the sale of goods or services ¿ Receipts for the sale of loans; debt or equity instruments in a trading portfolio ¿ Interest received on loans ¿ Dividends received on equity securities ¿ Payments to suppliers for goods and services ¿ Payments to employees or on behalf of employees Items which are added back to the net income figure (which is found on the Income Statement) to arrive at cash flows from operations generally include:¿ Depreciation (loss of tangible asset value over time) ¿ Deferred tax ¿ Amortization (loss of intangible asset value over time) ¿ Any gains or losses associated with the sale of a non-current asset; because associated cash flows do not belong to the operating section

series.name: Net cash flows from investing activities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Cash flow from investing activities is an item on the cash flow statement that reports the aggregate change in a company's cash position resulting from any gains (or losses) from investments in the financial markets or in operating subsidiaries and changes resulting from amounts spent on investments in capital assets such as plant and equipment.

series.name: Net cash flows from financing activities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This category in a company¿s cash flow statement shows that that accounts for external activities allow a firm to raise its capital or repay its investors through activities such as issuing cash dividends; adding or changing loans or issuing more stock. Cash flow from financing activities shows that investors have confidence on company¿s financial strength. A company that frequently turns in to new debt or equity for cash could have problems if the capital markets become less liquid.

series.name: Total capital employed of non-financial listed companies
series.description: The total of shareholders¿ equity and total non- current liabilities engaged in the capital formation constitute this item. Total capital employed = Shareholder's equity+ Long term secured loan+ Long term unsecured loan+ Debentures/ TFC's+ Employees benefit obligations.

series.name: Retention in business  of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This is the amount that a company retains in business after netting off all possible expenses and is obtained by deducting the provision for the tax and the total dividend distributed or proposed to be distributed from the net profit for the year.  Retention in business = Net profit before taxes- Tax provision- Total amount of dividend

series.name: Depreciation for the year  of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It includes all the depreciation charged to the profit and loss account. Owing to absence of uniform accounting standards; depreciation is a subjective item and varies from company to company. It is important for an analyst to know what effect such variation could have on the net profit.

series.name: Salaries; wages and employee benefits of non-financial listed companies
series.description: These are salary; wages and employees benefit expenses that a company has borne in all stages to run the business activities. These covers the expenses to all employees (temporary; permanent)

series.name: Total fixed liabilities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It is the sum total of the items debentures (TFC¿s) and other fixed liabilities Total fixed liabilities = Long term secured loan+ Debentures/TFC's

series.name: Contractual liabilities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This item pertains to all secured debentures; long-term loans; finance lease; short term secured loans and bank overdraft. Contractual liabilities = Long term secured loan+ Preference shares+ TFC's + Short term secured loans.

series.name: Purchases incl. cost of sales and inventories of current year of non-financial listed companies
series.description: A temporary account used in the periodic inventory system to record the purchases of merchandise for resale. (Purchases of equipment or supplies are not recorded in the purchases account.) Purchases= Cost of sales (current year) + inventories (current year) ¿ inventories (previous year)

series.name: Operating cash flow of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Operating Cash Flow (OCF) is the amount of cash generated by the regular operating activities of a business within a specific time period. OCF begins with net income. Operating Cash Flow = EBIT + Depreciation ¿ Taxes

series.name: No. of Non-financial companies listed at PSX
series.description: Total number of companies covered in the analysis for the year.

series.name: Net Profit  margin / Net profit to sales  of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Net profit margin reflects that part of profit which is left for the owners from the rupee of sales after all expenses and taxes paid.

series.name: Asset turnover  of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Asset turnover ratio measures the company's ability to utilize its total assets in generating sales or revenues.

series.name: Return on Assets of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Return on Assets measures the percentage of profit of a company in relation to its overall resources i.e. assets. It measures how efficiently company is using its assets to generate earning.

series.name: Financial leverage of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Financial Leverage describes the share of the capital injected in an enterprise with reference to the amount of the total assets.

series.name: Return on equity of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Return on equity appraises the efficiency of a company in terms of utilizing its shareholders equity for seeking profit.

series.name: Gross profit  margin of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Gross profit margin is the basic measure to assess a firm's financial health by revealing the proportion of money left over from sales after accounting for the cost of goods sold.

series.name: Operating return on assets of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Operating income synonym for Earnings Before Interest and Tax (EBIT) is a useful measure to gauge the company's profitability. Operating Return on Assets determines the operating income generated in comparison to the each rupee invested in total assets of the company in percentage.

series.name: Return on capital employed of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) measures a company's profitability and the efficiency with reference to the capital employed; where capital employed is non-current liabilities and shareholders? equity.

series.name: Current ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: The current ratio is a liquidity ratio that measures a company's ability to pay its obligations over the next 12 months.

series.name: Quick ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: The quick ratio also known as the acid-test ratio is a strong indicator of whether a firm has sufficient short-term assets to cover its immediate liabilities. This metric is more robust than the current ratio; also known as the working capital ratio; since it ignores less liquid assets such as inventory.

series.name: Cash to current liabilities of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Cash ratio is defined to determine how quickly a company can repay its short term debt. It is obtained by dividing the total cash and cash equivalents to its current liabilities.

series.name: Inventory Turnover Ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Inventory turnover shows how many times a company's inventory is sold and replaced over a period.

series.name: No. of days in inventory ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Days in inventory also known as Days Inventory Outstanding is an efficiency ratio that measures the average number of days the company holds its inventory before selling it. The ratio measures the number of days funds are tied up in inventory.

series.name: Receivables turnover ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Receivables turnover ratio measures how efficiently a firm use its assets. It helps to quantify firm's effectiveness in extending credit and in collecting debts on that credit. Normally; the companies do not segregate their sales into credit and cash. So the net sales are taken as a proxy of net credit sales to calculate account receivable turnover.

series.name: No. of days in receivables ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: A measure of the average number of days that a company takes to collect revenue after a sale has been made.

series.name: Payable turnover ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Payable turnover ratio measures the rate at which a company pays off to its suppliers.

series.name: No. of days in payable ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: No of days payable is company's average payable period. Days payable outstanding or no. of days in creditors tells how long it takes a company to pay its invoices from trade creditors; such as suppliers.

series.name: Working capital turnover ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Working capital turnover assess how effectively a company is using its working capital to generate sales.

series.name: Cash conversion cycle ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: The cash conversion cycle (CCC) is a metric that expresses the length of time; in days; that it takes for a company to convert resource inputs into cash. The cash conversion cycle attempts to measure the amount of time each net input rupee is tied up in the production and sales process before it is converted into cash through sales to customers. This metric looks at the amount of time needed to sell inventory; the amount of time needed to collect receivables and the length of time the company is afforded to pay its bills without incurring penalties.

series.name: CS operations to sales ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: This ratio compares the operating cash flows of a company to its sales. Cash flow from operations to sales indicates the ability of a company to generate cash from its sales.

series.name: Cash return on assets ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Cash Return on Assets calculates how much cash flow from operation is generated from the total assets of the company.

series.name: Cash return on equity ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Cash Return on Equity refers to how much cash flow generated in terms of the equity injected in the company.

series.name: Cash to income ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Cash to Net Income is a ratio used to determine the quality of a firm's reported earnings.

series.name: Debt coverage ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: It provides information on how much cash the company generates from operations that could be used to pay off the total debt. Total debt includes all interest-bearing debt; short and long term.

series.name: Paid up value of shares of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Paid up value of a share is the actual price of a share paid by the shareholders of a company.

series.name: Market price per share of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Market value represents the price at which a share is traded in stock market. Market value greater than its paid up value signify the positive gesture for investors.

series.name: Basic earnings per share of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Basic earnings per share provide an estimate of the amount to be distributed to each share of the outstanding stock from company's net income. Earnings per share also help to gauge the profitability of the company.

series.name: Price earnings ratio  of non-financial listed companies
series.description: The Price-to-Earnings Ratio or P/E ratio is a ratio for valuing a company that measures its current share price relative to its per-share earnings.

series.name: Dividend payout ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: The percentage of earnings paid to shareholders in dividends is the dividend payout ratio. It is calculated as:

series.name: Cash dividend per share of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Dividend per share (DPS) is the total dividends paid out over an entire year (including interim dividends but not including special dividends) divided by the number of outstanding ordinary shares issued.

series.name: Book value per share of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Book value per share is a measure used by owners of common shares in a firm to determine the level of safety associated with each individual share after all debts are paid off.

series.name: Debt equity ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Debt/Equity Ratio helps to ascertain the financial leverage of the company. It indicates how much debt a company is using to finance its assets relative to the amount of value represented in the shareholders equity. This form of D/E may often be referred to as risk or gearing.

series.name: Debt to assets ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Total debt to total assets is another leverage ratio that defines the total amount of debt relative to assets. This enables comparisons of leverage to be made across different companies. The higher the ratio; higher the degree of leverage; and consequently the financial risk.

series.name: Debt to capital ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: A measurement of a company's financial leverage; calculated as the company's debt divided by its total capital.

series.name: Interest cover ratio of non-financial listed companies
series.description: Interest cover ratio is used to determine how easily a company can pay interest on outstanding debt. It is achieved by dividing the company's earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) during a given period by the amount a company must pay in interest on its debts during the same period.

series.name: Growth Rate of Real Gross Domestic Product
series.description: Growth Rate of Real Gross Domestic Product with respect to previous year.

series.name: Gross Domestic Product (Total of Gross Value Addition at Constant Basic Prices(2005-06))
series.description: Gross domestic product (GDP) is equal to the sum of the gross value added of all the institutional units resident in national territory engaged in production (that is; gross value added at constant basic prices).

series.name: Commodity Producing Sector
series.description: Commodity producing sector includes agricultural and industrial sectors of the economy. It is the most significant component of the economy as it has stronger forward and backward linkages for economic growth and development of the country.

series.name: Agricultural Sector
series.description: Agriculture sector consists of crops; livestock; fishing and forestry sub-sectors.

series.name: Industrial Sector
series.description: Industry is the second major component of the commodity producing sector of the economy. It has multi-dimensional direct and indirect linkages; which have spillovers effects on the economy. Industrial sector generates demand for agriculture produce using it as raw materials and also provides supplies of latest machineries and tools to modernize other sectors of the economy. It is a major source of tax revenues and also contributes in the provision of job opportunities to urban and rural labour force.

series.name: Services Sector
series.description: Services sector includes Transport; Storage and Communication; Wholesale and Retail Trade; Finance and Insurance; Housing Services (Ownership of Dwellings); General Government Services (Public Administration and Defense); and Other Private Services (Social Services) subsectors.

series.name: Weighted-average Overnight Repo Rate
series.description: Overnight Repo Rate is the volume-weighted average rate of all money-market overnight repo deals. In an overnight repo deal;  a financial institutions sells government securities with an agreement to repurchase the securities on next working day. Such dealings are extensively used to manage short-term wholesale liquidity.

series.name: State Bank of Pakistan's Reverse Repo Rate
series.description: Formally known as rate on SBP 3-Day Repo Facility. Since August 17; 2009 Via DMMD Circular # 01 of 2009; it was replaced with SBP O/N Reverse Repo Rate. With effect from August 17; 2009 Via DMMD Circular # 01 of 2009; it serves as a Ceiling for SBP Interest Rate Corridor.

series.name: State Bank of Pakistan's Repo Rate
series.description: Introduced with effect from August 17; 2009 Via DMMD Circular # 01 of 2009; it serves as a Floor for SBP Interest Rate Corridor.

series.name: State Bank of Pakistan's Policy (Target) Rate
series.description: Introduced with effect from May 25; 2015 Via DMMD Circular # 09 of 2015; as new Policy (Target) Rate.

series.description: Branchless banking operations are either carried through OTC or M-Wallets. Within OTC; agents constitute the major portion which are retail shops; franchises; mobile shops and others of each BB entity. Any agent that has carried out at least one transaction in last 90 days is categorized as active.

series.name: Total Number of Branchless Banking Accounts
series.description: Branchless banking accounts are opened; maintained and operated through licensed BB operators. They are usually categorized in L0; L1 & L2 accounts and can be opened through mobile apps or Agent locations. This is the total number of Branchless Banking accounts nationwide.

series.name: Risk Weighted Capital Adequacy Ratio of Development Finance Institutions
series.description: Capital adequacy and availability ultimately determine the degree of robustness of Development Finance Institutions to withstand shocks to their balance sheets.

series.name: TIER1 Capital to Total Risk Weighted Assets of the Development Finance Institutions
series.description: The ratio measures the capital adequacy of Development Finance Institutions based on core capital concepts of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.

series.name: Total Eligible Capital to Total Assets of the Development Finance Institutions
series.description: The ratio indicates the extent to which assets are funded by their own funds and is a measure of capital adequacy of the Development Finance Institutions. It also measures financial leverage and is sometimes called the leverage ratio.

series.name: Non-Performing Loans to Total Loans of the Development Finance Institutions
series.description: This FSI is calculated by using the value of NPFs as the numerator and the total value of the loan portfolio (including NPFs; and before the deduction of specific loan loss provisions) as the denominator. This FSI is often used as a proxy for asset quality and is intended to identify problems with asset quality in the fund portfolio.

series.name: Provisions to Non-Performing Funds of the Development Finance Institutions
series.description: The FSI gauges the extent to which the NPFs are already covered by specific and general provisions allocated by the Development Finance Institutions.

series.name: Net Non-Performing Funds to Net Financing of the Development Finance Institutions
Net Non-Performing Funds to Total Capital of the Development Finance Institutions
series.description: The ratio indicates the extent to which assets are funded by their own funds and is a measure of capital adequacy of the Development Finance Institutions. It also measures financial leverage and is sometimes called the leverage ratio.

series.name: Investment in Equities to Total Eligible Capital of the Development Finance Institutions
Return on Assets before Tax of Islamic Banking Institutions
series.description: This FSI is calculated by dividing net income before extraordinary items and taxes (as recommended in the FSI Guide) by the average value of total assets (financial and nonfinancial) over the same period. This FSI is an indicator of bank profitability and is intended to measure the Islamic Banking Institution's efficiency in using their assets.

series.name: Return on Assets After Tax of the Development Finance Institutions
series.description: This FSI is calculated by dividing net income after extraordinary items and taxes (as recommended in the FSI Guide) by the average value of total assets (financial and nonfinancial) over the same period. This FSI is an indicator of bank profitability and is intended to measure the Development Finance Institution's efficiency in using their assets.

series.name: Return on Equity before Tax of the Development Finance Institutions
series.description: This FSI is calculated by dividing net income before extraordinary items and taxes by the average value of capital over the same period. Capital is measured as total capital and reserves as reported in the sectoral balance sheet; for cross-border consolidated data; Tier 1 capital can also be used. This FSI is a profitability indicator and is intended to measure the Development Finance Institution's efficiency in using their capital.

series.name: Return on Equity after Tax of the Development Finance Institutions
series.description: This FSI is calculated by dividing net income after extraordinary items and taxes by the average value of capital over the same period. Capital is measured as total capital and reserves as reported in the sectoral balance sheet; for cross-border consolidated data; Tier 1 capital can also be used. This FSI is a bank profitability indicator and is intended to measure the Development Finance Institution's efficiency in using their capital.

series.name: Net Markup Income to Gross Income of the Development Finance Institutions
series.description: This FSI is calculated by using net markup income as the numerator and gross income as the denominator. It is a profitability ratio; which measures the relative share of net markup earnings¿markup earned less markup expenses¿ within gross income. In the case of the Development Finance Institution's with low leverage; this FSI will tend to be higher.

series.name: Operating Expenses to Gross Income of the Development Finance Institutions
series.description: This FSI is a profitability ratio; which measures the size of administrative expenses within gross income¿that is; it measures the efficiency of Development Finance Institution's use of resources.

series.name: Trading Income to Gross Income of the Development Finance Institutions
series.description: This FSI is calculated by using gains or losses on financial instruments as the numerator and gross income as the denominator. It is an indicator of earnings and profitability; which is intended to capture the share of the Development Finance Institution's income from financial market activities; including currency trading¿that is; it measures the bank's reliance on market-related activity to generate profits.

series.name: Personnel Expenses to Non-Markup Expenses of the Development Finance institutions
series.description: This FSI is an indicator of earnings and profitability. It provides an indication of efficiency as a high or increasing ratio could undermine profitability.

series.name: Liquid Assets ratio of Development Finance Institutions
series.description: This FSI is calculated by using the core measure of liquid assets as the numerator and total assets as the denominator. The ratio can also be calculated using the broad measure of liquid assets as the numerator. This FSI is a liquid asset ratio; which provides an indication of the liquidity available to meet expected and unexpected demands for cash. The level of liquidity indicates the ability of the Development Finance Institutions to withstand shocks to their balance sheet.

series.name: Liquid Assets to Total Deposits of the Development Finance Institutions
series.description: This FSI is calculated by taking the value of nonperforming loans (NPLs) less the value of specific loan provisions as the numerator and capital as the denominator. Capital is measured as total capital and reserves in the sectoral balance sheet; for cross-border consolidated data; total regulatory capital can also be used. This FSI is a capital adequacy ratio and is an important indicator of the capacity of the deposit takers to withstand losses from NPLs.

series.name: Liquid Assets to Short-Term Liabilities of the Development Finance Institutions
series.description: This FSI is calculated by using the core measure of liquid assets as the numerator and short-term liabilities as the denominator. The ratio can also be calculated by taking the broad measure of liquid assets as the numerator. This FSI is a liquid asset ratio and is intended to capture the liquidity mismatch of assets and liabilities; and provides an indication of the extent to which deposit takers can meet the short-term withdrawal of funds without facing liquidity problems

series.name: Advances to Deposits ratio of the Development Finance Institutions
Customer Deposits to Total Financing of the Development Finance Institutions
series.description: This FSI is sometimes used to detect liquidity problems¿a low ratio might indicate potential liquidity stress in the banking system; and perhaps a loss of depositor and investor confidence in the long-term viability of the sector.
