This FSI is a capital adequacy ratio and is an important indicator of the capacity of Microfinance Bank's capital to withstand losses from NPLs.

series.name: Return on Assets Before Taxes of Microfinance Banks
series.description: This FSI is calculated by dividing net income before extraordinary items and taxes (as recommended in the FSI Guide) by the average value of total assets (financial and nonfinancial) over the same period. This FSI is an indicator of bank profitability and is intended to measure deposit takers¿ efficiency in using their assets.

series.name: Return on Assets After Taxes of Microfinance Banks
series.description: This FSI is calculated by dividing net income after extraordinary items and taxes (as recommended in the FSI Guide) by the average value of total assets (financial and nonfinancial) over the same period. This FSI is an indicator of bank profitability and is intended to measure deposit takers¿ efficiency in using their assets.

series.name: Return on Equity Before Taxes of Microfinance Banks
series.description: This FSI is calculated by dividing net income before extraordinary items and taxes by the average value of capital over the same period. Capital is measured as total capital and reserves as reported in the sectoral balance sheet; for cross-border consolidated data; Tier 1 capital can also be used. This FSI is a bank profitability indicator and is intended to measure deposit takers¿ efficiency in using their capital.

series.name: Return on Equity After Taxes of Microfinance Banks
series.description: This FSI is calculated by dividing net income after extraordinary items and taxes by the average value of capital over the same period. Capital is measured as total capital and reserves as reported in the sectoral balance sheet; for cross-border consolidated data; Tier 1 capital can also be used. This FSI is a bank profitability indicator and is intended to measure deposit takers¿ efficiency in using their capital.

series.name: Net Interest Income to Gross Income of Microfinance Microfinance Banks
series.description: This FSI is calculated by using net interest income as the numerator and gross income as the denominator. It is a profitability ratio; which measures the relative share of net interest earnings¿interest earned less interest expenses¿ within gross income. In the case of Microfinance Banks with low leverage; this FSI will tend to be higher.

series.name: Net Interest Margin of Microfinance Banks
Non-Interest Expense to Gross Income of Microfinance Banks
series.description: This FSI is a profitability ratio; which measures the size of administrative expenses within gross income¿that is; it measures the efficiency of Microfinance Bank¿s use of resources.

series.name: Administrative Expenses to Total Expenses of the Microfinance Banks
series.description: The FSI is a profitability ratio; which measures the size of the administrative expenses in the total expenses of the Microfinance Banks.

series.name: Operational Self Sufficiency of Microfinance Banks
series.description: The FSI measures the ability of the Microfinance Banks to generate financial revenues to cover their total costs.

series.name: Cost per Borrower of Microfinance Banks
series.description: Operating Expensesper average number of outstanding borrowers.

series.name: Liquid Asset Ratio of Banks of Microfinance Banks
series.description: This FSI is calculated by using the core measure of liquid assets as the numerator and total assets as the denominator. The ratio can also be calculated using the broad measure of liquid assets as the numerator. This FSI is a liquid asset ratio; which provides an indication of the liquidity available to meet expected and unexpected demands for cash. The level of liquidity indicates the ability of the Microfinance Banks to withstand shocks to their balance sheet.

series.name: Liquid Assets to Deposits of Microfinance Banks
series.description: The ratio measures the value of liquid assets with respect to total deposits of the Microfinance Banks

series.name: Liquid Assets to Short-term Liabilities of MFBs
series.description: This FSI is calculated by using the core measure of liquid assets as the numerator and short-term liabilities as the denominator. The ratio can also be calculated by taking the broad measure of liquid assets as the numerator. This FSI is a liquid asset ratio and is intended to capture the liquidity mismatch of assets and liabilities; and provides an indication of the extent to which Microfinance Banks can meet the short-term withdrawal of funds without facing liquidity problems

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Currency and Deposits
series.description: This is the sum of currency; transferable deposits; restricted and other deposits.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Currency Holding
series.description: NBFIs holding of currency in hand as most liquid assets to meet their operations need.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Transferable Deposits
series.description: NBFIs Transferable deposits as assets is deposits held in the deposit accounts; and NBFIs may withdraw deposits without any restrictions.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Restricted Deposits
series.description: NBFIs restricted deposits as assets is deposits held in the accounts and NBFIs may not withdraw deposits without regulatory compliance. For example: NBFIs' deposits may be time restricted deposits.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Other Deposits
series.description: NBFIs Other deposits as assets are deposits held in the accounts which are not classified elsewhere. For example: NBFIs' deposits may be time restricted deposits.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Investment in securities other than shares
series.description: This is the sum of short and long term investments by NBFIs in securities other than shares

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Investment in securities other than shares - Short-term
series.description: Investments by NBFIs in securities other than shares with less than or equal to one-year maturity. NBFIs hold securities issued by residents and non-residents Financial Corporations (FCs) as assets.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Investment in securities other than shares - Long-term
series.description: Investments by NBFIs in securities other than shares with more than one-year maturity. NBFIs hold securities issued by residents and non-residents Financial Corporations (FCs) as assets.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Loans extended (Advances)
series.description: It is the sum of short and long term loans

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Loans extended (Advances) - Short-term
series.description: NBFIs loans to the borrowers for short-term. NBFIs may have given loans as advances to Financial institutions (Fis).

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Loans extended (Advances) - Long-term
series.description: NBFIs loans to the borrowers for Long-term. NBFIs may have given loans as advances to Financial institutions (Fis).

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Investment in shares
series.description: It is the sum of quoted and non-quoted investments

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Investment in shares - Quoted
series.description: NBFIs holding of shares of listed companies through stock exchange companies.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Investment in shares - Non quoted
series.description: NBFIs holding of shares of non-listed companies.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Insurance Technical Reserve
series.description: It is the sum of life and non-life insurance .

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Insurance Technical Reserve Assets - Life
series.description: NBFIs' life insurance technical reserves consist of prepayments of net life insurance premiums and reserves to meet outstanding life insurance claims.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Insurance Technical Reserve Assets - Non-life
series.description: NBFIs Nonlife insurance technical reserves consist of prepayments of net nonlife insurance premiums and reserves to meet outstanding nonlife insurance claims.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Financial Derivatives
series.description: NBFIs holding of financial  Derivatives as assets. For example: NBFIs may have Forward Currency Swaps.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Other accounts receivable
series.description: NBFIs Other accounts receivable include assets of NBFIs not classified elsewhere. For example: trade credit and advances.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Non-financial assets
series.description: Non-financial assets; is the sum of Produced and Non-Produced Assets

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Non-financial assets - Produced assets
series.description: Non-Financial assets; is the sum of NBFIs' Fixed assets; Inventories; Valuables and Other Produced Assets.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Produced assets - Fixed assets
series.description: Fixed assets¿assets that are used repeatedly; or continuously; in production processes for more than one year (dwellings; other buildings and structures; machinery and equipment; and cultivated assets; such as livestock for breeding and plantations; and intellectual property products).

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Produced assets  - Inventories
series.description: Inventories (materials and supplies; work-in progress; finished goods; and goods for resale).

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Produced assets - Valuables
series.description: Valuables (assets that are acquired and held primarily as stores of value).

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Other produced assets
series.description: Other produced assets include assets that are not included in the above categories of the produced assets.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Non-produced assets
series.description: No produced assets is the sum of Land and Other Non-Produced Assets

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Non-produced assets  - Land
series.description: naturally occurring assets such as land; water; uncultivated forests.

series.name: NBFIs Assets: Other-non-produced assets
series.description: NBFIs Other-non-produced assets include assets which are not classified elsewhere.

series.name: NBFIs Total Assets  / Liabilities
series.description: Sum total of all assets of NBFIS; both financial and non-financial assets.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Deposits
series.description: Deposits is the sum of Restricted and other deposits

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Restricted deposits
series.description: Restricted deposits are those for which withdrawals are restricted on the basis of legal; regulatory; policy; or commercial requirements.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Other deposits
series.description: Other deposits include deposits which are not included elsewhere.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Securities other than shares (bonds/debentures etc.)
series.description: Security other than shares ( Bonds and Debentures) is the sum of short and long term securities other than shares

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Securities other than shares (bonds/debentures etc.) - Short-term
series.description: Short-term debt security (one-year or less than one-year) that gives the holder the unconditional right to fixed payments or contractually determined variable payments on a specified date or dates. NBFCs issue Bonds and Debentures for the investors. the investor may be an individuals and or corporations. this is liability of the issued NBFC and its total is reported in this head.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Securities other than shares (bonds/debentures etc.) - Long-term
series.description: Long-term debt security (more than one-year) that gives the holder the unconditional right to fixed payments or contractually determined variable payments on a specified date or dates. NBFCs issue Bonds and Debentures for the investors. the investor may be an individuals and or corporations. this is liability of the issued NBFC and its total is reported in this head.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Loans (Borrowings)
series.description: Loans and Borrowing is the sum of short and long term loans and borrowing.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Loans (Borrowings) - Short-term
series.description: This includes loans and borrowing of NBFCs; for period of one-year or less than one-year.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Loans (Borrowings) - Long-term
series.description: This includes loans and borrowing of NBFCs; for period of more than one-year.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Financial Derivatives
series.description: NBFIs may issue financial  Derivatives as liabilities. For example: NBFIs may have Forward Currency Swaps.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Other accounts payable
series.description: Other accounts payable of NBFIs include liabilities not classified elsewhere.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Shares and other equity (listed and non-listed shares) issued by NBFIs.
series.description: Shares and other equity is the sum of Quoted; Non-Quoted; retained earing; current year results; general and special reserves and valuation adjustments.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Shares and other equity - Quoted
series.description: Shares and other equity (listed also referred as quoted shares) issued by NBFIs.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Shares and other equity - Non quoted
series.description: Shares and other equity (listed also referred as non-quoted shares) issued by NBFIs.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Retained earnings
series.description: The category of retained earnings shows all earnings (after-tax profit) from the overall operations of the NBFI less any amount allocated to general and special reserves; which is established as a capital cushion to cover operational and financial risks of the NBFIs.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Current year result
series.description: Accumulated revenues during the year minus expenditures minus taxes minus retained earnings minus general and special reserves minus dividend payable are the current year result of the NBFI.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: General and special reserves
series.description: General and special reserves are capital redemption reserve; profit prior to incorporation; share premium; statutory reserves and appropriations of retained earnings. General and Special reserves should be valued as the nominal amount of earnings that have been retained.

series.name: NBFIs Liabilities: Valuation adjustments
series.description: Valuation adjustment represents the net counterpart of all changes (Surplus / deficit on revaluation) in the values of assets and liabilities on the balance sheets of the banks except for valuation changes recorded in the profit and loss accounts. The valuation adjustment is market valued by definition.

series.name: NBFI Time Deposits of Scheduled Banks
series.description: Scheduled Banks deposits in NBFCs as time-deposits.

series.name: NBFI Time Deposits of Non Financial Public Sector Enterprises
series.description: Non Financial Public Sector Enterprises deposits in NBFCs as time-deposits. For example; Pakistan Railways and Pakistan Post Office Department; etc deposits their cash amount in NBFCs as time-deposits.

series.name: NBFI Time Deposits of Non-Bank Financial Institutions
series.description: Non-Bank Financial Institutions deposit in NBFCs as time-deposits. For example; modaraba companies; investment banks; Development Finance Institutes (DFIs) and venture capital companies; etc place their cash amount in NBFCs as time-deposits.

series.name: NBFI Time Deposits of Insurance Companies
series.description: Insurance Companies deposits in NBFCs as time-deposits. For example; EFU insurance companies and State Life insurance companies; etc deposit their cash amount in NBFCs as time-deposits.

series.name: NBFI Time Deposits of Private Corporate Business
series.description: Private Corporate Business deposits in NBFCs as time-deposits. For example; TRG and Telenor Pakistan ; etc deposit their cash amount in NBFCs as time-deposits. the corporations may be listed and non-listed companies.

series.name: NBFI Time Deposits of Un-incorporated Enterprises and Individuals
series.description: Un-incorporated Enterprises and Individuals deposits in NBFCs as time-deposits. For example; Safari enterprise is an unincorporated company and it deposits its cash amount in NBFCs as time-deposits. the corporation is non-listed company. any individual can deposit its cash amount in the NBFCs as time-deposits.

series.name: NBFI Time Deposits of Federal Government
series.description: Federal Government deposits in NBFCs as time-deposits. For example; Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Finance; etc deposit their cash amount in NBFCs as time-deposits.

series.name: NBFI Foreign Currency Deposits
series.description: This is the total amount of Foreign Currency (FCY) deposits held by NBFCs.

series.name: NBFI Foreign Currency Deposits of Residents
series.description: FCY deposits of residents with NBFCs. The resident is generally defined as an individual and or corporation whose economic interests is in the economy where it resides; for at least last one-year.

series.name: NBFI Foreign Currency Deposits of Non-Residents
series.description: FCY deposits of Non-residents with NBFCs. The non-resident is generally defined as an individual and or corporation whose economic interests is not the economy where it invests and or deposits its FCY; for at least last one-year.

series.name: NBFI Bonds and Debentures
series.description: Bonds and Debentures are defines as; Long-term debt security that gives the holder the unconditional right to fixed payments or contractually determined variable payments on a specified date or dates. NBFCs issue Bonds and Debentures for the investors. the investor may be an individuals and or corporations. this is liability of the issued NBFC and its total is reported in this head.

series.name: NBFI Borrowing/Finance Lease Obligation
series.description: This is the sum of amount of Borrowing/Finance Lease Obligation from the different sources.

series.name: NBFI Borrowing from Federal Government
series.description: NBFCs loans (liabilities) from any federal government institutions. For example; Federal government sometimes sanctions loan schemes for growth of NBFCs.

series.name: NBFI Borrowings from State Bank of Pakistan
series.description: NBFCs loans (liabilities) from State Bank of Pakistan (SBP). For example; NBFCs avail loans and financing from SBP.

series.name: NBFI Borrowing/Finance Lease Obligation from Scheduled Banks
series.description: NBFCs loans (liabilities) from Scheduled Banks. For example; NBFCs avail loans and financing from scheduled banks.

series.name: NBFI Borrowing/Finance Lease Obligation from Non-Bank Financial Institutions
series.description: NBFCs loans (liabilities) from Non-Bank Financial Institutions (NBFIs). For example; NBFCs avail loans and financing from NBFIs.

series.name: NBFI Borrowing from Insurance Companies
series.description: NBFCs loans (liabilities) from Insurance Companies. For example; NBFCs avail loans and financing from Insurance companies.

series.name: NBFI Borrowing from Financial Institutions Abroad
series.description: NBFCs loans (liabilities) from Financial Institutions Abroad (FIA). For example; NBFCs avail loans and financing from FIA .

series.name: NBFI Borrowing/Finance Lease Obligation from Others
series.description: NBFCs loans (liabilities) from other sources. Others include all borrowing/financing sources except mentioned above.

series.name: NBFI Money at Call in Pakistan
series.description: Money at call is defined as Funds placed with a financial institution (here NBFCs) without a fixed maturity date. The money can be ¿called¿ (withdrawn) at any time.¿ It is a form of clean borrowing / lending in the MM for short term requirements without collateral. Transactions are based entirely on trust and goodwill of the players. in case; NBFCs borrow from money market as call money; it is reported in this head.

series.name: NBFI Other Liabilities
series.description: Other Liabilities of NBFCs include all liabilities not included in the above.

series.name: NBFI Total Capital and Liabilities
series.description: Total Capital and Liabilities

KSE All Index of the last working day of the month.
series.description: The KSE all share indexes was constructed and introduced on September 18; 1995. This is also a total return index (dividend; bonus and adjusted rights shares) computed for all companies listed at KSE. Please be noted that the data corresponds to the last working day of the month.

series.name: KSE 100 Index of the last working day of the month.
series.description: The KSE-100 Index was introduced in November 1991 with base value of 1;000 points. The Index comprises of 100 companies selected based on sector representation and highest market 178 capitalization; which captures over 80% of the total market capitalization of the companies listed on the Stock Exchange. One company from each sector based on the largest market capitalization and the remaining companies are selected based on largest market capitalization in descending order. This is a total return index i.e. dividend; bonus and rights are adjusted. Please be noted that the data corresponds to the last working day of the month.

series.name: Market Capitalization of the last working day of the month.
series.description: The Market Capitalization is the total market value of ordinary shares comprising the General Index. The market value is worked out by multiplying the market price by the total number of shares outstanding and added together for the component groups as also for the entire list to compile the series. Please be noted that the data corresponds to the last working day of the month.

series.name: National CPI; an Inflation Measure (Year-on-Year basis)
series.description: National CPI; an Inflation Measure (Year-on-Year basis). Urban and Rural CPIs are used to compile National CPI. Weighted Geometric Mean is computed to obtain National CPI; using proportion of urban and rural consumption received through Household Integrated Income and Consumption Survey (HIICS) as their respective weights.

series.description: Urban CPI; an Inflation Measure (Year-on-Year basis). The Urban CPI for the base year 2015-16 covers 356 items in the basket of goods and services; which represent the taste; habits and customs of households living in urban areas of Pakistan collected from 68 markets spread over 35 cities across Pakistan.

series.description: Commodity producing sector includes agricultural and industrial sectors of the economy. It is the most significant component of the economy as it has stronger forward and backward linkages for economic growth and development of the country.

series.name: Agricultural Sector
series.description: Agriculture sector consists of crops; livestock; fishing and forestry sub-sectors.

series.name: Industrial Sector
series.description: Industry is the second major component of the commodity producing sector of the economy. It has multi-dimensional direct and indirect linkages; which have spillovers effects on the economy. Industrial sector generates demand for agriculture produce using it as raw materials and also provides supplies of latest machineries and tools to modernize other sectors of the economy. It is a major source of tax revenues and also contributes in the provision of job opportunities to urban and rural labour force.

series.name: Services Sector
series.description: Services sector includes: Transport; Storage and Communication; Wholesale and Retail Trade; Finance and Insurance; Housing Services (Ownership of Dwellings); General Government Services (Public Administration and Defense); and Other Private Services (Social Services).

series.name: Gross Domestic Product (Total of Gross Value Addition at Constant Basic Prices(2015-16))
series.description: Gross domestic product (GDP) is equal to the sum of the gross value added of all the institutional units resident in national territory engaged in production (that is; gross value added at constant basic prices).

series.description: Agriculture sector consists of crops; livestock; fishing and forestry sub-sectors.

series.name: Industrial Sector
series.description: Industry is the second major component of the commodity producing sector of the economy. It has multi-dimensional direct and indirect linkages; which have spillovers effects on the economy. Industrial sector generates demand for agriculture produce using it as raw materials and also provides supplies of latest machineries and tools to modernize other sectors of the economy. It is a major source of tax revenues and also contributes in the provision of job opportunities to urban and rural labor force.
